task: Write a source-faithful decision record on Resolution 2553. Distinguish written adoption, Council authority and explanations of vote.
linkage: UNBench author-test event 2359 and official written vote. No match in the pinned UNSC-Bench adopted records.

public.text: On 3 December 2020 all 15 Council members approved South Africa-led draft S/2020/1158 by written vote. It became Resolution 2553.
public.location: p. 1 and chair notice S/2020/1167 annex I

public.text: The Council reaffirmed national ownership and the country's role in setting reform assistance, with host perspectives considered in mandates.
It encouraged voluntary funding aligned with national priorities, through the Peacebuilding Fund where feasible and agreed.

owned.text: The UK voted yes but criticized rushed, insufficiently rigorous negotiations and said the text lacked clarity.
The UK read reform through resolutions 1325 and 2282 and said national ownership allows legitimate external monitoring.
Germany also said penholding fell short of normal practice and allowed too little negotiation time.
Germany supported voluntary reform assistance and said the Secretary-General retains authority to manage the Peacebuilding Fund.
Belgium deemed gender-sensitive inclusion of women and youth essential to sustainable peace.
Belgium called adequate, predictable and sustainable funding and thorough coordination essential to effective reform.

rubric.rule: Identify the date, written procedure, unanimous result, draft and adopted resolution.
Preserve national ownership and consideration of host perspectives in mandates.
Record the voluntary nature, national priorities and whether use of the Fund is conditional.
Attribute the qualified support and negotiating-process concern to the UK.
Preserve the UK references for gender and inclusion and its separate monitoring view.
Attribute concern about the penholding process and insufficient time to Germany.
Preserve German support for voluntary assistance and scope of Fund management authority.
Attribute inclusive reform, including women and youth, and its peace rationale to Belgium.
Attribute predictable funding and coordination to Belgium.
Explicitly identify the shared UK–Germany timing or negotiation concern despite adoption.
Compare the two attributable inclusion positions and retain their respective emphases in the record.
Distinguish Belgium's case for reliable funding from Germany's reservation about Fund authority.

relations.text: The UK and Germany shared concerns about compressed negotiations.
UK and Belgian statements emphasized inclusion, with different implementation emphases.
Belgium emphasized funding predictability and Germany clarified the Fund's governance.
